question: The left button over the map whole - press, drag, release - the drag box and what it takes, the keys behind input slots 10, 11 and 12, a click and a Shift-click on a counter, a stack, a port or an air base, the right click with several selected, the counters' rings, and the keys that act on the selection.
slots_noted: The Keyboard_* bodies sit in the keyboard object's table at 0x1608494, which has no RTTI and so is in no class's table the merge knows; their slots are given in each comment. CInGameIdler slot 96 (0x6439E0, mov eax,[ecx+0x1314]) is described under the +0x1314 field and not recorded as a function.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_HandleInput
addresses.revises: Read whole for the selection wave: the drag box, the click and the Shift-click, Ctrl, the right click with several selected, the group keys and the other keys. Corrects FINDINGS-provinceview.md A.1 on the box's modifier: input slot 11 (Alt) held cancels the box outright; what keeps the old selection is Shift, and only where unit rows exist.
addresses.comment: **The in-game screen's handler for the mouse and keys over the map**, called once a frame from CInGameIdler::Update (0x656471), `ret 4`. First, anything selected whose kind (selectable slot 1) is 9 - the CSelectable default, which no class with RTTI answers - clears the selection (slot 46). Then +0x1DD4 = MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer (the thing under the pointer) and +0x1DD0 = the province under it, and the frame's input events (+0x1CB0; event +0 key code, +4 Windows message 0x100 key down or 0x102 character, +8 0 mouse or 1 key, +0x10 3 press or 4 release, +0x14 button 1 left 2 right, +0x18 handled byte, +0x20 next) are walked in order. **Left press** (not handled): +0x1300 = 1, +0x12F4 = the ground point under the pointer (CMap 0x492850), the down byte +0x12E0 = 1. **Left release with the down byte set** (no handled test): the right-click menu (+0x1D90) hidden, +0x12E0 = 0, and CInGameIdler_IsDragging decides. *A click* (not a drag): a deployment being placed is posted first where it may be (FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md B.4, unchanged); otherwise +0x1314 = the thing under the pointer, and with Shift (keyboard slot 10) and something under it: already selected - Selection_Remove (selection_changed where it was an air unit); not selected and Selection_CanAdd - added without clearing; otherwise with anything selected nothing at all. Without Shift (or with nothing under the pointer): the side menus and the orders view closed, Selection_Clear, the unit rows (+0xD20) freed, selection_changed, 0x66B7B0, an open country view toggled shut, then the thing selected where Selection_CanAdd allows; with Ctrl (keyboard slot 12) and an army (kind 0) CUnit::SelectSubordinates; without Ctrl, the deploy menu reopened where exactly one thing is selected and the clear had closed it. +0x12E4 = -1 after any add. *A drag*: in map mode 17 the box gives provinces to a theatre (CUpdateTheatreCommand of the list +0x6C); otherwise **Alt (keyboard slot 11) held does nothing at all**; else the selection is cleared as for a click (no selection_changed, no deploy-menu reopen) unless Shift is held and unit rows exist (+0xD28), and then three walks of the player's country's units (CCountry +0xBAC, every level): land units in a land province, then fleets, then air units, each taken where its map position (slot 30) lies within the box between the two ground points grown by 2 on every side and Selection_CanAdd allows - so the first unit taken fixes the kind and land wins; +0x12E4 = -1 for each. +0x1300 = 0, and 0x663400 outside mode 17. **Right release**: with nothing selected, no rows and the left button up, the province right-click menu (0x6754B0). Then, with +0x1CE0 clear and a province under the pointer: an orders view up and shown gets its slot 4 (province, Shift); otherwise, unless a visible interface element is under the mouse (gui +0x98, +0x43), **every selected thing in selection order gets its slot 6 (province, Shift)** - CUnit::OrderToProvince for units. **Keys**: Pause (key down) or Space (character) outside multiplayer slot 27 (the pause, *inferred*, not read); the console on 0xA7 or '`'; **'0' to '9' CInGameIdler_SelectionGroupKey**; '+' and '-' slots 25 and 26 (the speed, *inferred*); Home (KeyEvent_IsHomeDown) slot 47 with the player's capital; the code 0x12 - Alt pressed, or Ctrl+R typed - outside mode 17 with a theatre headquarters of the player's selected alone (CInGameIdler::GetSelectedUnit, oob_level 0) slot 110, not read; 'h' render_hierarchy (FINDINGS-hierarchy.md); Escape (key down) clears the selection (slot 46) or else 0x66BD10(0). There is no double click: nothing here reads a clock. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x652540-0x653984 (ret 4 at 0x6538C5 and 0x653984, int3 after), with the decompilation of a copy carrying the record beside it. The box: 0x652DCF slot 0x2C then jne 0x653236 skips both the clear and the three walks; 0x652DE1-0x652DF6 clear unless [+0xD28] != 0 and slot 0x28; the three walks 0x652E91 (slot 0x3C and path node +0x22), 0x652FF4 (not 0x3C, not 0x44), 0x653134 (not 0x3C, not 0x40), each comparing slot 0x78's two ints +-2 against [esp+0x30]/[esp+0x3C] and [esp+0x38]/[esp+0x44], the min/max of +0x12F4/+0x12FC and the release point made at 0x652C1D-0x652C83. The click: 0x6532AE-0x6534DF. The right click: 0x6534E4-0x6535C6, push al (slot 0x28) and the province (graphics +0xC) to each node's [vt+0x18]. Wrong if the event layout is misread - the press arm's +0x10 == 3 and +0x14 == 1 against the release arm's 4 and 1/2 is the control.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_IsDragging
addresses.no_signature: the in-game screen in ESI, no stack arguments, a bare `ret`, the answer in AL
addresses.comment: **Whether the left button held is a drag.** False unless +0x1300 (set by the left press) is set; otherwise the ground point now under the pointer (mouse object +0x64 slot 19, CMap 0x492850) less the press's (+0x12F4, +0x12F8, +0x12FC), and true where the length of that three-figure difference is **2.0 or more** (the float literal at 0x1718064; `fcompi` with `ja` to false, so exactly 2.0 is a drag). Map units, not pixels: the further out the camera, the shorter the move on screen. Asked by the release (0x652BCB), the cursor (0x6539B3), the frame's drawing of the box (0x65718B) and slot 34 (0x663AC9). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x64D850-0x64D94F on the listing: cmp byte [esi+0x1300],0; the subtractions at 0x64D8B4-0x64D908 against [esi+0x12F4/F8/FC]; call 0x402000 (sqrt) on the sum of squares; fld [0x1718064] (2.0f, read from the image) fcompi; ja to the false exit. Four callers by findRefs. Wrong if 0x492850 answers screen coordinates rather than map ones - but its x and z are what the box compares with units' map positions.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_DrawSelectionBox
addresses.comment: **The drag box on the map**, drawn every frame while CInGameIdler_IsDragging holds (one caller, 0x657197, in the frame's drawing). Five points at height 0 - the press's ground point (+0x12F4, +0x12FC) and the one now under the pointer, (x1,z1) (x2,z1) (x2,z2) (x1,z2) (x1,z1) - **a closed outline on the ground, square to the map's axes**, not to the screen; drawn with the ID3DXLine at +0x1CCC - SetWidth(2.0), so **two pixels wide**, Begin, DrawTransform(the 5 points, the map's translation (-+0x1C74, -+0x1C78) times the camera's view and projection, the colour), End - with depth test and depth writes off (render states 7 and 14 set 0, back to 1 after); colour **white**, CColor(1,1,1,1) brightened by 1.1 and clamped (0x643750), packed. In map mode 17 the colour is the selected theatre's (its region's, 0x486EB0), or (0.8,0,0) where it is not in the country's list, and the provinces the player controls whose label point falls in the box (+-2) are coloured and gathered into +0x6C as the drag goes - what the release posts in a CUpdateTheatreCommand. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x64D9FE-0x64DAAB writes the five float triples at [ebp-0xD8]..[ebp-0xA0] from +0x12F4, +0x12FC and the point 0x492850 answers; 0x64DCC3 pushes 5 and [ebp-0xD8] to the line object's slot 6; the floats 0x171DBAC (1.0), 0x160A2F0 (1.1) and 0x174C564 (0.8) read from the image; ret 4 at 0x64E14B. +0x1CCC is made by D3DXCreateLine (the import at 0xD2B440, called at 0x65D13E in CInGameIdler::Enter), so slots 4, 6, 11 and 17 are ID3DXLine's Begin, DrawTransform, SetWidth and End by the interface's documented order.

addresses.name: MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer
addresses.no_signature: the map's graphics owner (CInGameIdler slot 15) in EAX; on the stack the mouse point (two floats), the selection list and an out int for the province id; `ret 0xC`; the selectable in EAX
addresses.comment: **What a click or the tooltip finds under the pointer**, in this order: the province under it (0x8558F0 over the owner's +0x1DC4; none where the owner's +0x1DE4 is 0) - its id to the out argument; **a battle's marker** in that province, then in each neighbour by the template's edge order (ProvinceGraphics_HitTestBattles); **the counters and the building pictures** of the province (ProvinceGraphics_HitTest, which also cycles a stack), then of each neighbour - a hit there gives the out id the neighbour's; else the province itself (its CSelectable at +8). Null with no province. Called by CInGameIdler_HandleInput every frame for +0x1DD4 and by 0x6F045D. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x6416D0-0x6418A2: the 0x8558F0 call guarded by [edi+0x1DE4]; 0x640DA0 at 0x64173C then in the edge loop (stride 0x14, the template's +0x90/+0x94) at 0x641793; 0x640F40 at 0x6417D9 then in the same loop at 0x641838 with the out id rewritten at 0x641883; the province pointer plus 8 at 0x641877. Three ret 0xC.

addresses.name: ProvinceGraphics_HitTestBattles
addresses.no_signature: the graphics owner in EDI; on the stack the province graphics and the mouse point; `ret 8`; the battle's CSelectable (combat + 8) or 0 in EAX
addresses.comment: **A click on a battle's marker.** Nothing with the camera above 500 (+0x348 of the owner's +4 against the double 500.0 at 0x160A538). Otherwise each 3D object of the province graphics' list (+0x10, then +0xDC, next +0xD8) is hit-tested (slot 20); **the first** that answers above 0 and is shown (slot 15) is looked for among the province's battles (CMapProvince +0x2EC) as a battle's +0x2C or +0x30, and that battle's selectable (+8, kind 7) is answered - selecting it opens its window (CCombat::OnSelected). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x640DA0-0x640F33: comisd against [0x160A538] = 500.0 (read); the object walk 0x640E99-0x640F1B; cmp [ecx+0x2C],esi / [ecx+0x30],esi over the list at [province+0x2EC], which the record names `combats`; lea eax,[ecx+8]; two ret 8.

addresses.name: ProvinceGraphics_HitTest
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall ProvinceGraphics_HitTest(void* owner, void* provinceGraphics, float* mouse, CList* selection)
addresses.revises: The counters' walk read through, which is where a click on the selected unit's own counter cycles to the next unit of the province; and the cleanup settled - all three exits are `ret 0x10` (0x641608, 0x641678, 0x6416A2), the 12 the old entry had being the next function's.
addresses.comment: **What a click on a province's pictures picks** (MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer asks it after the battles). The large air base picture (+0x7C) offers the air base's selectable (CMapProvince +0x54, +0x18; kind 8), the large naval base picture (+0x80) the CPort (+0x354; kind 4), the higher score winning. **sel**: where exactly one thing is selected, of kind 0, 1 or 2, and its own avatar (+0x164) is under the mouse. With the camera at 500 or under, each 3D object of the province (+0x10, +0xDC, next +0xD8) scoring above the best so far: where the counters are on (settings word bit 0x800), the province's unit vector (+0x2C8) at its cursor (+0x2E8) is asked - with the camera above counter_distance and that unit not selected and not at its own base, it alone (intel 2 or more) is taken where this object is its avatar; otherwise the vector is walked round from the cursor, and **with sel every unit in sel's province, of sel's owner and not at its own base is gathered in that order** and the walk stops; without sel the unit whose avatar this object is wins. Then, where the buildings are on (bit 0x20), the object shown and the province not hidden by fog, a building picture (+0x40 vector) offers the CPort for a naval base, the air base's selectable for an air base, the building (kind 6) otherwise. **With sel the answer is the unit after sel in what was gathered, wrapping** - so clicking the one selected unit's counter again picks the next of its owner's units in the province; sel alone answers itself. Otherwise the best hit, or 0. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x640F40-0x6416C9, three ret 0x10 (0x641608, 0x641678, 0x6416A2); the last block (0x6416A5) is the bad_alloc throw, `call 0xB9894B` and then int3 to 0x6416CF - checkSignatures still reports 12 and 16 because its walk does not stop at the throw and runs into MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer's ret 0xC. The cycle: [ebp-0x18] set at 0x641176 only for a count of 1 and kinds 0/1/2 and cleared at 0x6411D5 where the avatar's score is not above 0; the gathering 0x6413F0-0x641473 (province +0x130 and owner +0x128 equal to sel's, 0x5CDC30 false, push through 0x6434C0); the answer 0x641585-0x641678, (index + 1) mod count. Inferred because what the province's +0x2C8 vector and +0x2E8 cursor hold is read from their writers (0x4A5880, 0x4A5DE3, CUnit::OnDeselected) and not from every one; a screenshot sequence - one division of a stack of three selected, its counter clicked twice - would show the cycle.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_SelectionGroupKey
addresses.comment: **The selection groups, '0' to '9'.** With Ctrl (keyboard slot 12) and unit rows (+0xD28 not 0): the id (+0x10, +0x14) of each row's unit (+0xD20, row +0x28), in row order, posted as a CSelectionGroupCommand(the player, ids, group) - nothing where no row exists. Without Ctrl, where +0x12E4 is this group, rows exist, something is selected and the first selected is a unit (kind 0, 1 or 2): **the camera is put on the first selected unit's province** (slot 48, CentreOnProvince) and nothing else. Otherwise: side menus and orders view closed, Selection_Clear, rows freed, 0x66B7B0, an open country view toggled shut outside a tutorial; then each id of the player's group (CCurrentGameState +0xD40, (country id x 10 + group) x 0x10) found (FindPersistentById), not already selected, and passing its slot 2 (the player's own) is selected (CSelectable_Select) unless it differs in kind from the first selected; +0x12E4 = group. Called only from CInGameIdler_HandleInput, for a key event whose code is '0'..'9': a plain digit arrives as a character, Ctrl and a digit as a key down (the window procedure posts key downs while Ctrl is held). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x664A60-0x664E84, three ret 8: slot 0x30 compared with 1 at 0x664A8E; the rows walk at 0x664AB9 reading [row+0x28]+0x10/+0x14; 0x5EA500 at 0x664BD4 with [0x1A89790]+0xC30 in ECX and the group pushed; the double-press arm 0x664C15-0x664CA5 calling slot 0xC0 with [first+0x130]; the store of the group to +0x12E4 at 0x664E6D. Caller by findRefs (one, 0x65363F, after cmp cl,0x30 / 0x39).

addresses.name: CUnit::SelectSubordinates

CInGameIdler_HandleInput calls it for a Ctrl-click on an army (kind 0) once that army is selected; 0x74DB5B and 0x7572C8 also call it. Bare `ret`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x5D36A0-0x5D37C2: [esi+0x1E4] walked by node +8; slot 0x3C of child and parent compared at 0x5D36F6; cmp byte [ebx+4],0 then [g_CCurrentGameState]+0xBE8's [vt+0x98] (slot 38) with the child; the recursive call at 0x5D37A4 reached from both arms. Three callers by findRefs.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_UpdateCursor
addresses.comment: **The mouse pointer over the map**, one caller (0x656660). Each case sets a pointer through the application's (+0x1790) +0xE4 slot 4 with a number: **3 while a drag is under way** (CInGameIdler_IsDragging); otherwise by what is selected and the province under the pointer - 4 over an interface element, 10 or 11 where a deployment being placed may or may not go there, 12 for a unit with an AI agent above it, and 5 to 8 for where a selected unit would go (8 boarding a port or a carrying fleet, 7 an enemy's, 6 allowed, 5 not). addresses.name: Keyboard_IsShiftDown
addresses.comment: **Input slot 10 is Shift.** `mov al,[ecx+0x50]` - the key-down byte of VK_SHIFT (0x10) in the keyboard's array at +0x40, indexed by virtual-key code. Slot 10 of the keyboard object's table 0x1608494 (no RTTI), which is what CInGameIdler +0x1C holds. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The bytes at 0xB4E120 and the table 0x1608494 + 10*4 = 0x16084BC holding 0xB4E120; the table is written only by 0xB4DFF0, made by the platform factory's keyboard slot 0xB08800; CInGameIdler +0x1C is the object UpdateMapCamera asks the arrow keys of through slot 9 (0xB4E160, [vk+0x40]), its own table's slot. Wrong if +0x1C held an object of another table - no other table holds 0xB4E160.

addresses.name: Keyboard_IsCtrlDown
addresses.comment: **Input slot 12 is Ctrl.** `mov al,[ecx+0x51]` - the key-down byte of VK_CONTROL (0x11). Slot 12 of the keyboard's table 0x1608494. Settles FINDINGS-scrollbar.md's `likely`, and the key FINDINGS-seaair.md section 1 left unnamed for the land orders window. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The bytes at 0xB4E130; 0x1608494 + 12*4 = 0x16084C4 holds 0xB4E130.

addresses.name: Keyboard_IsAltDown
addresses.comment: **Input slot 11 asks for Alt - by VK_LMENU or VK_RMENU (0xA4, 0xA5, bytes +0xE4 and +0xE5), which nothing found ever sets.** 1 or 0 in EAX. Slot 11 of the keyboard's table 0x1608494. The keyboard's only setter (Keyboard_OnKeyMessage) stores at the message's own key code, and Windows reports either Alt key as VK_MENU (0x12), which lands at +0x52; so this is *inferred* always false, and the drag box's Alt test with it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The bytes at 0xB4E140 (cmp [ecx+0xE4],0; cmp [ecx+0xE5],0); 0x1608494 + 11*4 = 0x16084C0 holds it. The negative: every store into the 256-byte array in the class's bodies (0xB4DFF0 constructor zeroing, 0xB4E090 clearing, 0xB4E0D0 [wParam+0x40] and +0x52) - control: the same reading finds VK_SHIFT and VK_CONTROL's stores through the wParam path; the image imports no MapVirtualKey or GetKeyboardState. A screenshot cannot show it; Alt held through a drag that still selects would.

addresses.name: Keyboard_IsKeyDown

addresses.evidence: The bytes at 0xB4E160 (mov al,[eax+ecx+0x40]; ret 4); 0x1608494 + 9*4 = 0x16084B8 holds it.

addresses.name: Keyboard_OnKeyMessage
addresses.signature: bool __fastcall Keyboard_OnKeyMessage(void* keyboard@ECX, int message@stack:4, int vk@stack:8, int lparam@stack:12) @AL

Nothing else is set and nothing is cleared here. True always; `ret 0xC`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0xB4E0D0-0xB4E112 (two ret 0xC); 0x1608494 + 4*4 = 0x16084A4 holds it; the window procedure's calls of [vt+0x10] with 0x100, 0x104 and 0x102 pushed (0xA917E4, 0xA91951, 0xA91A4C).

addresses.name: Keyboard_ForgetReleasedKeys
addresses.comment: Slot 5 of the keyboard's table 0x1608494: for each of the 256 key codes, the held byte (+0x40) cleared where GetAsyncKeyState says the key is up, and the pressed byte (+0x140) cleared outright; +0x240 cleared. So a key reads down from its message until the first pass after it is let go. Answers 1, bare `ret`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0xB4E090-0xB4E0CB: the call through [0xD2B298] (GetAsyncKeyState by the import table) in a loop to 0x100; 0x1608494 + 5*4 = 0x16084A8 holds it.

addresses.name: KeyEvent_IsHomeDown
addresses.no_signature: the input event in EAX, a bare `ret`, the answer in AL
addresses.comment: True where an input event is the Home key (code 0x24) and not a character message (+4 != 0x102). One of a row of such tests at 0xAB8B80-0xAB8CB0 (Pause, Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right, End, Left/Right with Shift). CInGameIdler_HandleInput puts the camera on the player's capital with it (slot 47). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: The bytes at 0xAB8C20-0xAB8C33: cmp dword [eax],0x24; cmp dword [eax+4],0x102; mov al,1 / xor al,al.

struct_fields.name: keyboard
struct_fields.comment: **The keyboard**: an object of the table 0x1608494 (no RTTI), 0x244 bytes, made by the platform factory's slot 2 (0xB08800). Its slots 10, 11 and 12 are the in-game screen's input slots - Shift, Alt (by VK_LMENU/VK_RMENU, never set), Ctrl - and slot 9 a key by code. UpdateMapCamera and the group keys ask it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: UpdateMapCamera's caller loads [ebx+0x1C] as the keys argument (0x656693); its slot 9 is 0xB4E160 only in that table.

struct_fields.name: left_down
struct_fields.comment: Set by a left press over the map that the interface did not take; cleared by the left release, which does nothing without it. A right release with nothing selected opens the right-click menu only while it is clear. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers 0x652871 (1), 0x652BC4 (0) and the constructor 0x648B7D; readers 0x652899, 0x652B9B, by a displacement sweep of .text (control: the press store found).

struct_fields.name: last_group
struct_fields.comment: The selection group last recalled by its digit, -1 once a click, a box or anything else adds to the selection. Pressing that digit again with it still in force puts the camera on the group's first unit instead of recalling it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: drag_start
struct_fields.comment: The ground point under the pointer at the left press, x, height, z (+0x12F4, +0x12F8, +0x12FC), from CMap 0x492850. One corner of the drag box; the drag test measures from it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Written at 0x652860/0x65286B from 0x492850's result; read by 0x64D8B9-0x64D8C9, 0x64D9FE, 0x652C0F.

struct_fields.name: drag_armed
struct_fields.comment: Set with left_down by the left press, cleared at the release; CInGameIdler_IsDragging answers false without it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: clicked
struct_fields.comment: The thing under the pointer while a click is being dealt with (copied from +0x1DD4), zeroed when it is done; slot 96 answers it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6532B4 writes [+0x1DD4]; 0x653319 and 0x6534D5 zero it; 0x6439E0 is mov eax,[ecx+0x1314].

struct_fields.name: input_events
struct_fields.comment: The frame's input events, oldest first, each {+0 key code, +4 message (0x100 key down, 0x102 character), +8 0 mouse / 1 key, +0x10 3 press / 4 release, +0x14 button 1 left / 2 right, +0x18 handled byte, +0x20 next}; CInGameIdler_HandleInput walks it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6526B7 loads it and 0x6538A2 follows +0x20; the window procedure builds the same records (0xA91803, 0xA91A69) with the message at +4 and 1 at +8 for keys.

struct_fields.name: selection_box_line
struct_fields.comment: An ID3DXLine, made by D3DXCreateLine in CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65D13E) and released by the destructor: what the drag box is drawn with, two pixels wide. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: lea ecx,[ebx+0x1CCC]; push ecx; push device; call [0xD2B440] (D3DXCreateLine by the import table) at 0x65D136; read at 0x64DA15, 0x64DAC1, 0x64DC93, 0x64DCFF in CInGameIdler_DrawSelectionBox; slot 2 (Release) at 0x6497CF.

struct_fields.name: province_under_pointer
struct_fields.comment: The province the pointer is over this frame, by the id MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer gives - a neighbour's where a counter or picture of the neighbour was hit; null off the map. Where the right click sends units and where a deployment is placed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.

struct_fields.name: hovered
struct_fields.revises: Named hovered_province: it is whatever MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer finds - a battle's, a unit's, a port's, an air base's or a building's selectable as well as a province's second table - so over a counter the map tooltip is the unit's own slot 3, not the province's.
struct_fields.comment: **The thing under the pointer**, made every frame by MapGraphics_PickUnderPointer: a battle's selectable (combat + 8), a unit, a CPort, an air base's selectable, a building, or the province's CSelectable (its second table, + 8). A click selects it; the map tooltip asks its slot 3 (ProvinceTooltip_Build for a province). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tooltips.md.
struct_fields.evidence: The only writers are 0x6525FA (0x6416D0's answer) and the constructor 0x6485DF, by a displacement sweep; 0x6416D0 answers 0x640DA0's, 0x640F40's or province + 8.

struct_fields.name: map_units
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of the units shown in the province (end +0x2CC), the order a click on the selected unit's own counter cycles through. *Inferred* from its readers (ProvinceGraphics_HitTest) and 0x4A5880, which finds a unit in it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x641313-0x641324 and 0x6413C8 read +0x2C8/+0x2CC as a vector of CUnit* (+0x1F8, +0x164, +0x130, +0x128 used); 0x4A58A0 searches it for EDI.

struct_fields.name: map_units_end
struct_fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x2C8. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Paired with +0x2C8 in every read: sub, sar 2.

struct_fields.name: map_unit_cursor
struct_fields.comment: An index into map_units: where a unit there is selected, its index (0x4A5880, at the head of CUnit::OnSelected); 0 when one is deselected (CUnit::OnDeselected); one less when a unit before it is taken out (0x4A5DE3). ProvinceGraphics_HitTest starts its walk there. *Inferred*. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Stores at 0x4A58B7, 0x4A5DEE, 0x5C0C06; read at 0x641319. Not every displacement hit at 0x2E8 is this field (CUnit and others use it); only those three were tied to a province by the register.

struct_fields.name: selection_group_array
struct_fields.revises: The comment said 0xA0 bytes an entry, indexed by the group's own id; the index is the country's id times ten plus the group, an entry is one 0x10-byte list.
struct_fields.comment: **The selection groups**: an array of 0x10-byte lists of unit ids (nodes of 0x14 bytes: type, id, previous, next), **ten per country** - the list for a country and a group is at (country id x 10 + group) x 0x10, so 0xA0 bytes a country. Written by CSelectionGroupCommand::Execute; read by CInGameIdler_SelectionGroupKey; what the `selectionGroups` loader writes into. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-selection.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x5EA67C-0x5EA688 (x5, x2, + group, x16, + [+0xD40]) and 0x664A60's recall reading [(group + id*10)*0x10] of the same pointer.
